analysis.one_liner: Bank of Baroda is a government-owned public sector bank, one of India's top three PSU banks by balance sheet size, serving retail, corporate and international banking customers.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 (quarter ended Sep 2026) results, reported in early November 2026, showed a record quarter: net profit of roughly ₹6,531 crore and net interest income up 9% YoY, alongside improving asset quality (gross NPA 1.78%, net NPA 0.37%). Management raised FY27 credit growth guidance to 13-15%. Separately, a July 2026 cyber breach reportedly exposed about 1TB of customer KYC and loan data on the dark web; the bank says core banking systems were unaffected but is raising security spend. No results or record date falls within the next two weeks - Q3 FY27 numbers are expected around January-February 2027.
analysis.plain_terms: Bank of Baroda is one of India's largest government-owned banks. The quarter just reported looks strong, with profit growth and shrinking bad loans, but the bank's own full-year return on equity (around 13%) is well below the 19%-plus annualised figure from this single quarter, so that strength should not be extrapolated. A more live concern is a July 2026 cyber breach where customer data was allegedly stolen and put up for sale, which the quarterly numbers don't capture. The stock trades below book value, but that is partly a structural PSU-bank discount rather than evidence of a bargain.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026): PAT of about ₹6,531-6,532 crore, up 35.8-38.8% YoY depending on source (standalone vs consolidated) - a record quarter, with NII up 9% YoY to ₹13,026 crore and operating profit up 50.9% YoY to ₹11,430 crore. Gross NPA improved to 1.78% (from 2.16% a year ago) and net NPA to 0.37%. NIM was 2.74% for the quarter (2.76% for H1 FY27). Quarterly-annualised ROA (1.26%) and ROE (19.28%) are well above the trailing-twelve-month figures from data aggregators (ROA ~0.89%, ROE ~12.7-13.68%), meaning this one strong quarter has not yet moved the full-year ratios. One aggregator shows H1 FY27 cumulative profit down ~16.5% YoY, which conflicts with the strong single-quarter number and could not be reconciled - treated as unverified. Management raised FY27 credit growth guidance to 13-15% and deposit growth guidance to 11-13%, kept NIM guidance at 2.75-2.95%, and guided credit cost below 0.6%.
analysis.performance_read: Over 5 years the stock is up 267% versus the Nifty's 48%, a strong run, but still well behind peer PNB's 326%. Over 3 years and 1 year too, Bank of Baroda has lagged PNB (60.65% vs 110.59% over 3 years; 2.6% vs 27.46% over 1 year) while beating the Nifty on both horizons. The stock is down 8.8% from its February 2026 peak of ₹314.28 and sits well above its 52-week low of ₹227.50. There was a 5:1 stock split in January 2015 - a share-count adjustment, not a price crash - which should already be reflected in the long-term return series supplied.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 6-7x and a price-to-book of 0.83x, the stock is cheap in absolute terms, which is typical for PSU banks - the market has long priced in government ownership, periodic equity dilution, and lower capital efficiency as a structural discount versus private banks. Whether that discount is still justified depends on whether the improved asset quality and record quarterly profit are sustainable, or whether this quarter marks a cyclical peak for a bank whose full-year ROE (near 13%) remains modest.
analysis.growth_read: Growth this quarter was both volume- and quality-led: NII rose 9% YoY on business expansion, and management raised FY27 credit growth guidance to 13-15%. Margins (NIM 2.74%) were roughly stable rather than expanding, so the profit jump came mainly from lower provisions and better asset quality rather than margin expansion - a more durable mix than a margin-only improvement, but one that depends on credit costs staying low (guided below 0.6%).
analysis.health_read: Asset quality has genuinely improved - gross NPA at 1.78% and net NPA at 0.37%, with a provision coverage ratio of 94.65%, meaning most bad-loan risk is already provided for. Capital adequacy is comfortable (CRAR 16.61%, CET1 14.20%). The bank still plans to raise up to ₹8,500 crore in fresh equity and ₹4,000 crore via AT1/Tier II bonds through FY28, normal for a growing PSU bank but a source of future dilution. The more pressing concern right now is operational/business risk rather than balance-sheet risk: a July 2026 cyber breach reportedly exposed about 1TB of customer KYC and loan data, a reputational and potential regulatory risk even though core banking systems were reportedly unaffected.
analysis.ownership_read: The Government of India holds 63.97% of Bank of Baroda, as is standard for a PSU bank, and this stake carries zero pledging - government holdings in PSU banks are not pledged. Domestic institutional holding is about 17.8-17.9%. Foreign institutional holding figures conflict sharply across sources (0.81% versus 10.29%), likely a classification difference between FII and broader FPI categories - not verified, check on Screener for the current breakdown. No single marquee outside investor was identified holding a notable disclosed stake.
strengths: Gross NPA improved to 1.78% and net NPA to 0.37% in Q2 FY27, down from 2.16%/0.57% a year earlier
Capital adequacy comfortable at CRAR 16.61% with CET1 of 14.20%
Record quarterly PAT of about ₹6,531 crore in Q2 FY27, with operating profit up 50.9% YoY
Trades at a P/B of 0.83x, below book value, with no pledging on the 63.97% government promoter stake
watchpoints: Full-year ROE (~13%) and ROA (~0.89%) are far below this quarter's annualised 19.28%/1.26% - one strong quarter should not be extrapolated
July 2026 cyber breach allegedly leaked ~1TB of customer KYC/loan data on the dark web; reputational and regulatory risk even if core banking was unaffected
Planned equity raise of up to ₹8,500 crore through FY28 will dilute existing shareholders to some degree
NIM of 2.74% is modest and management's own guidance range (2.75-2.95%) leaves little room for margin expansion; profit growth depends on credit costs staying below the guided 0.6%
analysis.one_thing: Whether improved asset quality (GNPA 1.78%, credit cost under 0.6%) and record profit hold up - the Q3 FY27 results, expected around January-February 2027, will show whether this quarter was a trend or a peak.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 operating figures (NII, PAT, NIM, GNPA/NNPA, CRAR) are drawn from the bank's own earnings-call transcript and treated as most authoritative. Third-party aggregators disagree on TTM P/E (6.21 vs 7.07), ROE (12.7% vs 13.68%), and FII shareholding (0.81% vs 10.29%) - flagged rather than averaged. A reported ~16.5% YoY fall in H1 FY27 cumulative profit from one aggregator conflicts with the strong single-quarter PAT growth and could not be reconciled; treated as unverified. CASA ratio (~37.2%) and specific large-investor holdings could not be fully verified - check on Screener.
